thread:
Priya: FYI saw cost attribution drift for a couple of large tenants. traced it to sampling mismatch when enrichment re-buckets cohorts after ingress sampling.
Jonah: are we still sampling at ingress only? or do we have any post-enrich sampling logic that could be changing the distribution?
Priya: ingress picks ~1% by trace_id mod but enrichment recomputes cohort and we sometimes re-evaluate sample decisions for downstream analytics. that re-eval changes cohort mix.
Ken: quick sketch: introduce an explicit stable sample token `sample_key` at ingress. use hash(sample_key) for sample decision and carry sample_key through enrichment. enrichment computes cohort but writes mapping (sample_key -> cohort) to a compact store. billing looks up cohort by sample_key.
Jonah: this avoids sampling flip-flops. downside: new header + mapping store.
Priya: agree its the safest. questions: header format, versioning, storage TTL, and backfill behavior.
Ken: header idea: `X-Sample-Key: v1:abc123xyz` (short base62 token). version prefix makes future changes safe.
Jonah: for backward compat we can default v1 to `trace_id` hashed to short token so older SDKs auto-work. then migrate SDKs to generate random tokens for better entropy.
Priya: storage: we need low-latency lookups for billing queries but durable trail for backfills. propose kafka topic writes from enrich -> small consumer populates redis cluster (TTL 7d) and batch-append to clickhouse for long-term.
Ken: that matches earlier chats. TTL needs to match longest billing lookback window + some buffer. 7d + 1d buffer seems reasonable.
Jonah: what about header size and proxy compatibility? keep token <=12 chars. test nginx/envoy limits; also add fallback so if header lost, enrich still computes cohort and marks `sample_key_missing=true` in mapping write.
Priya: good. we should also tag reconstructed mappings in clickhouse so billing can treat them as approximate. e.g., `reconstructed=true|false`.
Ken: collision risk: if token entropy low, same sample_key maps to multiple cohorts. plan: enrich should emit metric `sample_key_conflict{tenant,shard}` when mapping changes. treat high conflict rate as alert. first-writer-wins seems ok but we must detect flips.
Jonah: also consider reservoir sharding for very-high-cardinality tenants: bucket sample_key via `%N` to limit memory hot keys.
Priya: rollout plan: 1) spec header + version, 2) short spike: enrich writes mapping + local consumer populates redis in test cluster, 3) SDKs start setting header (default to trace-derived token), 4) enable billing lookups from mapping store, 5) switch SDKs to random tokens, 6) deprecate trace-derived default.
Ken: include migration for old traces: if `sample_key` absent, billing will attempt cohort decode heuristics then mark `cohort_approx=true`. backfill job can replay payloads to rebuild mappings and write `reconstructed=true`.
Jonah: testing matrix: header lost, version mismatch, redis miss (fallback to clickhouse), mapping TTL eviction during queries, conflict spike, reservoir hot-keys. add unit + integration tests.
Priya: perf numbers needed: expected mapping QPS = sampled_qps * sample_rate. Samir (cc) can help with traffic estimates.
infra-bot: created ticket INF-9044: "stable sample_key handshake + mapping store + reconciliation" -> https://go/internal/INF-9044
Ken: we should also document schema in observability handbook: header name, token format, mapping table columns, metrics emitted, and alert thresholds.
Jonah: one more ops note: add a debug endpoint to lookup sample_key->cohort for a given tenant/id to help support. auth gated.
Priya: OK I'll draft RFC with diagrams: header lifecycle, kafka -> redis -> CH flow, TTL sizing math, collision metrics, and rollout checklist. will link INF-9044.
Ken: thanks. I'll prototype the redis consumer and emit a few synthetic conflict metrics.
Jonah: I'll add envoy/nginx header compatibility tests to infra CI.
Priya: great. looping back once the RFC is up. :white_check_mark:
